cards.text: Then the LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, about the guilt offering, starting with someone who acts unfaithfully and sins unintentionally against any of the LORD's holy things. Unintentionally, huh? Friend, I once sealed a whole cookie box with the cookies still sitting on the counter.

He brings the LORD an unblemished ram from the flock as his guilt offering, of proper value by the sanctuary shekel. And for the holy thing he harmed, he makes restitution and adds a fifth of its value.

cards.question: For the holy thing he harmed, the man pays back its value plus a fifth. Who does he give it to?
Once the priest makes atonement for him with the ram, the man is forgiven.

cards.text: Next case: someone breaks one of the LORD's commandments, and he had NO idea he did it. Friend, that's me walking around the bakery all morning with flour in my eyebrows.

cards.question: Since the man didn't know he broke the LORD's commandment, he isn't counted guilty.

cards.text: He brings the priest an unblemished ram of proper value, and the priest makes atonement for the wrong he committed in ignorance. It's a guilt offering, and he was certainly guilty before the LORD.
Then the LORD speaks to Moses again. This time, the case is someone who deceives his neighbor.

cards.question: When someone deceives his neighbor, the LORD says he is acting unfaithfully against whom?

cards.text: It could be lying about something left in his care, stealing, extortion, or finding lost property and swearing falsely about it. And swearing falsely, friend, that's not a fib anymore, that's a fib in a SUIT AND TIE.

cards.question: When someone has cheated his neighbor and becomes guilty, what is his first step?

answers.text: He waits seven days in his tent
He tells the elders at the gate

cards.question: The man who cheated his neighbor can make it right whenever it's convenient after he admits his guilt.
He makes restitution in full, adds a fifth of the value, and pays it to the ___ on the day he acknowledges his guilt.

cards.text: Then he brings the priest his guilt offering to the LORD, an unblemished ram of proper value from the flock.

cards.question: When the priest makes atonement for the man who cheated his neighbor, how much is he forgiven for?

answers.text: None of it until the next year

cards.text: That's the guilt offering, friend. But the LORD isn't done teaching Moses about the offerings, so keep that apron on.
